description: Knowledge served through MCP: kb_list and kb_read, deterministic. A file is markdown unless its first line is a shebang naming another engine (raw, envsubst, mustache or a server's own); 'engines' (default envsubst and mustache) are the ones this server renders with. Kinds by id prefix. tools-: 'modes' (and 'limits') give the tools' names and input schemas. args-: a tool's 'arguments' are validated against 'modes' and 'limits'; expect the arguments with defaults, or an error class. list-, read-, plain-, envsubst-, mustache-, template-: a 'tool' call on 'overlays' (identity, manifest, tree as digest.json writes it, 'served', and the template 'facts' the consumer holds for it: root, state, scope, project and the user's options), with 'arguments', optional 'modes', 'limits' and the caller's 'facts' (caller, env, env_allow); expect the result or an error class. envelope-: a handler's outcome as MCP's tools/call result. plan-: whether an overlay's rules and context are left out of the context because they are served.

Every name an envsubst file reads: the five AOS_ names, the caller's role and profile, the allowed variables of the environment, the call's context (strings, integers and booleans, not a list), and the options. As GNU envsubst does, $$ is no escape (so $${X} is a dollar and the value), a Mustache tag is text, and a name with no value (a variable not allowed, a list, a sensitive option, an unknown name) stays as written, undefined=debug being the default.

As GNU envsubst: $NAME and ${NAME} are both read, a bare name as long as it goes.
By default (undefined=debug) a name with no value stays as written, bare or braced, as it does in aos.
GNU's has no defaults or other operators: '${NAME:-word}' is text, defined name or not.
GNU's has no $$ escape: '$$NAME' is a dollar and the value; a dollar before anything that is no name, and a brace never closed, are text.
'${NAME' with no brace is text, not a bare name.
A value is inserted as it is: a '$' in it is no reference.
undefined=lenient gives nothing for a name with no value, as GNU's own envsubst does.
undefined=debug, the default, written out: a name with no value is kept as it was written, as nginx's image does with $request_uri.
undefined=strict refuses a name with no value.

'.MARKDOWN' in ASCII capitals is markdown.
A file whose first-line option has a value it does not have cannot be served without a context to fail on: it is listed apart, with the reason 'render'; kb_read gives the error.
And reading it says why.
In the expanded format '$$' is '$' before anything, a name or not: '$$x' is '$x', '$$AOS_OVERLAY_NAME' is '$AOS_OVERLAY_NAME'.
A server on a Mustache library with no escape-off setting (a released tplx) cannot honour escape=none: the file is served as written, with the context, and is not an error.
The same server renders a file that asks for no option, and one that asks for escape=html.
escape=html is the library's own.
A server without the drone dialect serves a file that asks for it as written with the context.
Any option value counts: a server that cannot refuse an undefined name serves a strict file as written.
kb_list says a file whose option value the server cannot honour is not rendered, and one that asks for another value is.
A result is the same JSON as structuredContent and as the one text block; isError is false.
An error is {"error": {"class", "message"}} the same way, and isError is true. Only the class is compared.
